correctness.rationale: The chessboard connectivity bound gives simple connectivity at (4,4); Armstrong kills the quotient fundamental group because the generating transpose has a fixed rook vertex. Flag cardinalities are strictly increasing and preserved by transpose, so stabilizers fix each flag pointwise and the orbit-flag boundary has the usual alternating signs without multiplicities. My separate submask-based enumeration and integral row elimination of each boundary gave cell counts (125,586,768,300), verified the consecutive boundary products, and left only unit nonzero Smith entries, in numbers (124,462,300). Boundary-image saturation in each full chain group also gives saturation in the cycle subgroup. Hence the computed integral homology is free with ranks (1,0,6,0). Hurewicz provides six two-sphere maps, and homological Whitehead gives the asserted wedge.
residual_risks: The replay verifies chain algebra, not the external connectivity and orbit-space theorems. It makes no claim about other boards or equivariant homotopy.
